Store QGIS styles for a layer in a GeoPackage

Source: R/gq_gpkg_style_write.R
gq_gpkg_style_write.Rd

Writes one or more QML documents into a GeoPackage's layer_styles table, the table QGIS reads when a layer is opened from the file, so the layer arrives styled with no .qml beside it. One style is the default QGIS applies; the others are listed by name under the layer's Properties > Symbology > Style > Load Style... > From Database.

Usage

gq_gpkg_style_write(
  gpkg,
  layer,
  styles,
  default = names(styles)[1],
  description = NULL
)

Arguments

gpkg

Path to an existing GeoPackage.

layer

Name of a feature table in gpkg.

styles

A named character vector (or list of strings) of QML documents, such as gq_qgis_style() returns; names become the styleNames and must be unique and non-empty.

default

Name of the style QGIS applies when it opens the layer. One of names(styles); the first by default.

description

Optional descriptions, one per style, written to the description column. Empty by default.

Value

gpkg, invisibly.

Details

Rows are written with the twelve columns QGIS itself writes. The f_table_catalog and f_table_schema cells are empty strings, never NULL, because QGIS matches a row to its layer on all four f_* columns, and a NULL schema leaves the layer unstyled even though the row is there.

The table is written through GDAL (via sf), which registers it in gpkg_contents as an attributes table, as QGIS does: a layer_styles table that is not registered is invisible to QGIS in any GeoPackage that already carries another attributes table.

A style already stored for layer under one of the names in styles is replaced; styles stored under other names, and every other layer's styles, are kept. The style named by default becomes the layer's only default. When every style is already stored as given, nothing is written, so a second call leaves the file's bytes as they were.

See also

gq_qgis_style() to build a QML from a registry layer, gq_style_qml() for the QML files gq ships.

Examples

reg <- gq_reg_custom(system.file("registry", "reg_custom.csv", package = "gq"))

# a small line layer carrying both classification fields
segs <- sf::st_sf(
  rule_class = c("both", "first"),
  grade_class = c("0.6-0.8", "0-0.2"),
  geom = sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_linestring(matrix(c(0, 0, 1, 1), 2)),
    sf::st_linestring(matrix(c(1, 2, 1, 3), 2)),
    crs = 3005
  )
)
gpkg <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
sf::st_write(segs, gpkg, "segments", quiet = TRUE)

# rule class as the default style, grade class as a second named style
gq_gpkg_style_write(gpkg, "segments", styles = c(
  rule = gq_qgis_style(reg, "habitat_rule_comparison"),
  grade = gq_qgis_style(reg, "habitat_expected_use")
))

st <- sf::st_read(gpkg, "layer_styles", quiet = TRUE)
st[, c("f_table_name", "f_geometry_column", "styleName", "useAsDefault")]
#>   f_table_name f_geometry_column styleName useAsDefault
#> 1     segments              geom      rule         TRUE
#> 2     segments              geom     grade        FALSE
